hypotheses.claim: The Qwen3.5 vision/mmproj representation can serve as the single deep visual backbone for Frank, feeding both MVC familiarity routing and semantic decode escalation, eliminating a duplicate heavy Retina encoder.
hypotheses.falsifier: A matched dedicated lightweight feature encoder materially dominates Qwen feature reuse on open-set/familiarity calibration or total task/resource Pareto performance.

hypotheses.claim: Raw generative Qwen vision representations will need a tiny learned projection/readout for stable user-specific familiarity/open-set geometry, but not a second heavy semantic vision encoder.
hypotheses.evidence: Qwen's own Qwen3-VL-Embedding family uses an explicit embedding/retrieval objective and dedicated embedding model path rather than claiming arbitrary base-VLM hidden states are already calibrated retrieval vectors.
hypotheses.falsifier: Raw pooled Qwen3.5 mmproj descriptors match or beat projected/dedicated embeddings on held-out familiar/near-neighbor unknown fixtures under equal total budget.

hypotheses.claim: Vision-encode-only plus MVC can safely bypass the 4B language decoder on a material fraction of recurring visual states.
hypotheses.falsifier: Decoder bypass rate is too low to save material cost, or bypass increases false familiarity/task failures beyond tolerance.

hypotheses.claim: Delta-guided ROI plus adaptive image-token budgets reduce visual-cycle cost while preserving GUI grounding and task success better than full-frame deep decode every cycle.
hypotheses.falsifier: ROI/context loss causes enough off-ROI modal, layout or small-text failures that matched full-frame processing is Pareto-superior.

hypotheses.claim: A hybrid of event/change processing plus periodic/on-demand full anchors is more robust than pure change-only visual sensing.
hypotheses.falsifier: Anchors add measurable resource cost without reducing stale-state, hidden-context or recovery failures.

hypotheses.claim: Action/outcome-linked visual crops plus compact typed state outperform repeated full-screenshot history for Frank's action verification and future retrieval under equal context budget.
hypotheses.falsifier: Local memory repeatedly misses global context needed for correct later decisions and cannot be rescued cheaply by anchor retrieval.

hypotheses.claim: User-named visual entities can be learned more sample-efficiently by binding MVC visual prototypes to textual/name anchors in the same Qwen multimodal semantic space, while keeping sensor evidence separate from semantic labels.
hypotheses.origin: Interaction between Qwen native multimodality, Qwen3-VL unified multimodal embedding research, and Frank's GOLD user-label learning path.
hypotheses.falsifier: Text-anchor binding worsens instance-level discrimination/open-set calibration or causes semantic similarity to masquerade as visual identity.

hypotheses.claim: After a deterministic pixel/tile change gate, temporal distance in pooled Qwen visual features can estimate semantic-change magnitude and control whether full semantic decode is necessary.
hypotheses.falsifier: Feature distance is unstable across benign crop/resolution/antialiasing changes or fails to separate semantically meaningful from irrelevant visual changes.

hypotheses.claim: Abliteration can leave low-level visual representation behavior mostly stable while still changing end-to-end visual decisions through the text/semantic decoder; therefore mmproj-level MVC compatibility and end-to-end visual action competence must be tested as separate layers.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched hashes/feature probes show the visual representation itself changes materially across the compared model export or the decoder change has no measurable visual-decision effect.

hypotheses.claim: A high-confidence visual identity/state produced by MVC or Qwen-native perception can serve as an evidence-bound seed into UnifiedDB's Emergent Assembly Preprocessor, causing currently relevant relational memory to surface before full 4B semantic decoding.
hypotheses.origin: User proposal fused with executed UnifiedDB/EAP research and q23 MVC/Qwen feature-reuse work.
hypotheses.falsifier: Visual-seeded EAP does not improve context/task quality or causes unacceptable wrong-memory amplification relative to Qwen-only and direct-memory baselines.

hypotheses.claim: The complete visual-seed-resolution plus EAP ActiveAssembly path can be near-negligible in latency relative to Qwen multimodal encode/decode, making associative memory retrieval effectively a low-cost perceptual reflex even though it is not literally zero-latency.
hypotheses.evidence: Existing EAP synthetic receipts report microsecond-class compilation/update subpaths and ~1 ms class natural-language hybrid retrieval, but no target-PC perceptual end-to-end measurement yet.
hypotheses.falsifier: Seed resolution, synchronization, serialization, cache maintenance or retrieved-context prompt cost makes the end-to-end coupled path materially slower than simpler direct routes.

hypotheses.claim: Visual-seeded EAP context can reduce total Qwen reasoning cost by preassembling a bounded ActiveAssembly of relevant current relations, decreasing broad memory/context search and possibly decoder work.
hypotheses.falsifier: Retrieved context increases prompt/attention cost or distracts the model enough that total sensor-to-correct-decision cost rises.

hypotheses.claim: EAP-derived relational gaps and uncertainty can guide Retina/Qwen active sensing toward higher-value ROIs or resolutions, reducing visual tokens per verified action.
hypotheses.falsifier: A perception-only uncertainty/ROI policy performs equally well or better with less coupling, or memory-guided sensing creates confirmation-bias failures.

hypotheses.claim: The same UnifiedDB/EAP possibility compiler can serve visual perception, textual queries and action/recovery memory as one shared associative model-input substrate, avoiding modality-specific memory databases.
hypotheses.falsifier: Visual-temporal retrieval requires specialized recency/similarity/index semantics that materially outperform the shared EAP substrate under the same correctness/resource constraints.

hypotheses.claim: Wrong or stale visual memory anchors can be made fail-closed if perceptual seed receipts bind frame/source epoch, visual feature version, open-set evidence and exact current UnifiedDB refs before EAP propagation.
hypotheses.falsifier: Wrong high-confidence seeds or stale graph state still propagate misleading ActiveAssemblies often enough to bias downstream perception/action despite the proposed guards.

hypotheses.claim: The causal benefit of Frank-specific prior experience follows a measurable dose-response curve: at N=0 target-relevant Frank episodic experience PAR/EAP should provide no genuine experience advantage; as independent provenance-bound experience episodes accumulate, a reproducible effect may emerge only after a finite onset N, then saturate or become non-monotonic if stale/conflicting experience accumulates.
hypotheses.origin: User requirement to distinguish Frank-has-experience from Frank-has-no-experience and measure the minimum data volume at which the effect actually becomes useful.
hypotheses.experience_definition: One data point is one independent provenance-bound Frank episode with observed visual evidence/context and verified outcome; near-duplicate frames within one episode do not inflate N. Qwen pretrained knowledge is held constant and is not Frank experience.
hypotheses.falsifier: No reproducible net benefit appears within the tested independent-experience range, direct memory dominates EAP at the same N, or small-N gains disappear on state-variant/novel held-out cases or reverse as conflicting experience accumulates.
